types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being, typically identified by name. Also called Individual, Person, IndividualHuman. Examples: Ron Johnson, Rand Paul, Anthony Fauci, Kevin Ault.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Mentions are individual human names, aligning directly with schema.org's Person class.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: USNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United States. Also called US charity type, American non-profit category, US voluntary sector classification. Examples: a 501(c)(3) organization, a public charity, a private foundation.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

types.embedding_query_text: MedicalProduct: A pharmaceutical or biological product intended for diagnosis, cure, treatment, or prevention of disease. Also called Medication, Vaccine, TherapeuticAgent. Examples: Covid-19 vaccines.

chosen_type.label: Drug
chosen_type.justification: Covid-19 vaccines are pharmaceutical products, matching schema.org's Drug class.

candidates.label: MedicalTherapy
candidates.comment: A therapeutic medical procedure designed to prevent, treat, and cure human diseases and medical conditions. Also called medical treatment, healthcare intervention, therapy regimen. Examples: "pharmacotherapy", "behavioral therapy", "supportive therapy", "dialysis". Distinct from MedicalProcedure, which is a broader category including diagnostic procedures.

candidates.label: Drug
candidates.comment: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.

candidates.label: TherapeuticProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical procedure specifically intended to treat a health condition or improve a patient's well-being. Also called medical treatment, therapy, healing procedure. Examples: chemotherapy, physical therapy, surgical removal of a tumor.

candidates.label: FinancialProduct
candidates.comment: A FinancialProduct is a Service provided by financial institutions to consumers and businesses. Also called financial instrument, banking product, investment product. Examples: A savings account, a mortgage loan, an insurance policy, a mutual fund.

candidates.label: DietarySupplement
candidates.comment: A product taken orally that contains dietary ingredients intended to supplement the diet, such as vitamins, minerals, or herbs. Also called Nutritional supplement, health supplement, vitamin, herbal remedy. Examples: Multivitamin pills, fish oil capsules, protein powder, ginseng extract. Distinct from Drug, which is primarily for treating, preventing, or diagnosing disease.

types.embedding_query_text: Study: A systematic investigation to establish facts and reach new conclusions. Also called Research, Investigation, ClinicalStudy. Examples: vaccine safety monitoring system.

chosen_type.label: MedicalStudy
chosen_type.justification: The mention refers to a monitoring system, which is a type of medical investigation covered by MedicalStudy.

candidates.label: MedicalObservationalStudy
candidates.comment: A medical study that infers the effect of a treatment by observing a cohort of subjects over time, without investigator control over treatment assignment. Also called observational research, cohort study, epidemiological study. Examples: a study tracking health outcomes in smokers vs. non-smokers, a study on diet and disease incidence. Distinct from MedicalTrial, where subjects are randomly assigned to treatment groups.

candidates.label: MedicalTrial
candidates.comment: A medical study that uses a scientific process to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or procedures, typically with random allocation to groups. Also called clinical trial, randomized controlled trial, interventional study. Examples: a Phase 3 drug trial, a study comparing two surgical techniques, a vaccine efficacy trial. Distinct from MedicalObservationalStudy, where treatment assignment is not controlled by the investigator.

candidates.label: MedicalStudy
candidates.comment: A medical entity that is an umbrella type covering all kinds of research studies relating to human medicine or health. Also called clinical study, health research, medical investigation. Examples: a drug trial, an epidemiological survey, a patient registry. Distinct from MedicalScholarlyArticle, which is the publication of study results, not the study itself.

candidates.label: MedicalObservationalStudyDesign
candidates.comment: An enumeration of design models for observational medical studies. Also called observational study type, research design, epidemiological design. Examples: "CohortStudy", "CaseControlStudy", "CrossSectionalStudy".

candidates.label: MedicalStudyStatus
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing the status of a medical study. Also called study phase, research status, trial stage. Examples: "Recruiting", "Active, not recruiting", "Completed", "Terminated".

types.embedding_query_text: StatisticalRate: A percentage or ratio derived from statistical analysis of data. Also called Rate, Percentage, RiskRate. Examples: 12.6% miscarriage rate, 82% miscarriage risk.

chosen_type.label: MedicalRiskScore
chosen_type.justification: Percentage-based risk rates align with the MedicalRiskScore class for simplified risk assessment.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskScore
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a simple system summing risk factors to yield a score associated with prognosis. Also called clinical score, prognostic score, risk index. Examples: "CHAD score", "TIMI risk score", "APACHE II score". Distinct from MedicalRiskCalculator, which involves more complex mathematical calculations.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskCalculator
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a complex mathematical calculation, often requiring an online tool, used to assess prognosis. Also called prognosis calculator, risk assessment tool, clinical prediction model. Examples: a calculator for cardiovascular disease risk, a tool for predicting cancer recurrence. Distinct from MedicalRiskScore, which is a simpler sum of risk factors.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: StatisticalVariable
candidates.comment: A measurable statistical metric that can be observed at a place and time, defined by a population type and specific constraints. Also called statistical metric, data point, observable quantity, measurement variable. Examples: median height of female persons, average temperature in a city, count of news articles published daily. Distinct from StatisticalPopulation, which is the group being measured, not the measurement itself.

candidates.label: DrugPregnancyCategory
candidates.comment: A DrugPregnancyCategory is a MedicalEnumeration assessing the risk of fetal injury from a drug used by the mother during pregnancy. Also called pregnancy risk category, fetal risk classification. Examples: PregnancyCategoryA, PregnancyCategoryX, PregnancyCategoryD.

types.embedding_query_text: MedicalOutcome Examples: 104 spontaneous abortions, 700 completed pregnancies in third trimester.

chosen_type.label: MedicalStudyOutcome
chosen_type.definition: A quantitative result from a medical study, such as the count of spontaneous abortions or completed pregnancies.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents study outcomes as numerical results; a new subclass of MedicalStudy is needed.

candidates.label: DrugPregnancyCategory
candidates.comment: A DrugPregnancyCategory is a MedicalEnumeration assessing the risk of fetal injury from a drug used by the mother during pregnancy. Also called pregnancy risk category, fetal risk classification. Examples: PregnancyCategoryA, PregnancyCategoryX, PregnancyCategoryD.

candidates.label: MedicalStudyStatus
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing the status of a medical study. Also called study phase, research status, trial stage. Examples: "Recruiting", "Active, not recruiting", "Completed", "Terminated".

candidates.label: MedicalTrial
candidates.comment: A medical study that uses a scientific process to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or procedures, typically with random allocation to groups. Also called clinical trial, randomized controlled trial, interventional study. Examples: a Phase 3 drug trial, a study comparing two surgical techniques, a vaccine efficacy trial. Distinct from MedicalObservationalStudy, where treatment assignment is not controlled by the investigator.

candidates.label: MedicalTrialDesign
candidates.comment: An enumeration of design models for medical trials. Also called clinical trial design, trial methodology, study architecture. Examples: "RandomizedControlledTrial", "SingleBlindTrial", "DoubleBlindTrial", "CrossoverTrial".

candidates.label: MedicalObservationalStudyDesign
candidates.comment: An enumeration of design models for observational medical studies. Also called observational study type, research design, epidemiological design. Examples: "CohortStudy", "CaseControlStudy", "CrossSectionalStudy".

chosen_type.label: TimePeriod
chosen_type.definition: A specific duration or point in time, such as a year or month, used for temporal categorization.
chosen_type.justification: Schema.org's ServicePeriod and Schedule are too application-specific; TimePeriod is a general-purpose time range.

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a particular purpose or activity. Also called Institution, Association, Agency. Examples: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Foundation for Infectious Diseases, Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine, CDC.

chosen_type.label: MedicalOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Mentions are medical institutions, aligning with schema.org's MedicalOrganization subclass.

mentions: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

types.embedding_query_text: Event: A significant happening or occurrence. Also called Occurrence, Happening, Incident. Examples: Covid-19 pandemic.

chosen_type.label: Event
chosen_type.justification: The pandemic is a significant global occurrence, fitting schema.org's general Event class.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

types.embedding_query_text: Publication Examples: New England Journal of Medicine.

chosen_type.label: PublicationVolume
chosen_type.justification: The journal is a volume of a periodical, matching schema.org's PublicationVolume.

candidates.label: MedicalScholarlyArticle
candidates.comment: A scholarly article specifically within the medical domain. Also called medical journal article, clinical research paper, healthcare publication. Examples: a peer-reviewed article on a new drug, a research paper on surgical techniques, a review article on a disease. Distinct from ScholarlyArticle, which is a broader category for academic papers.

candidates.label: PublicationIssue
candidates.comment: A PublicationIssue is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or publication volume, often numbered and containing a grouping of works. Also called journal issue, magazine issue, periodical issue. Examples: "Nature" Vol. 500, Issue 1; "The New Yorker" October 26, 2023 issue; a specific issue of a scientific journal. Distinct from PublicationVolume, which is a larger grouping of issues.

candidates.label: MedicalObservationalStudyDesign
candidates.comment: An enumeration of design models for observational medical studies. Also called observational study type, research design, epidemiological design. Examples: "CohortStudy", "CaseControlStudy", "CrossSectionalStudy".

candidates.label: MedicalTrialDesign
candidates.comment: An enumeration of design models for medical trials. Also called clinical trial design, trial methodology, study architecture. Examples: "RandomizedControlledTrial", "SingleBlindTrial", "DoubleBlindTrial", "CrossoverTrial".

candidates.label: PublicationVolume
candidates.comment: A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume. Examples: "Nature" Volume 500; "Encyclopedia Britannica" Volume 1; a year's collection of a magazine. Distinct from PublicationIssue, which is a smaller, more granular part of a volume.
